title: Cold rebuild: A first-look profile
summary: Rebuild A first-look profile from memory, no hints.

steps.title: Cold rebuild
body: Time to prove a piece stuck. You built **A first-look profile** in *A first look at a dataset*. Now write it again from an
**empty editor**: no starter, no hints, no solution to peek at. The tests are exactly the ones you passed
Why: pulling something out of memory is what makes it stay there. Reading your old code feels like knowing
it; rebuilding it cold shows whether you do. If you get stuck, that is useful news: go back to the lesson,
then come back and try again tomorrow.
This check, plus the boss, is what proves the module.

steps.explain: Six rows, five columns. `qty` loaded as `float64`, not `int64`: one cell is empty, and an empty number becomes `NaN`, which is a float. A numeric column that is unexpectedly float often means missing values.

steps.title: Rebuild A first-look profile cold
prompt: Write `first_look(df)` that returns a dict describing any DataFrame:
"missing": {"qty": 1},             # only columns with at least one missing value
Values must be plain `int`s. `df.select_dtypes("number").columns` lists the numeric columns.
**From memory this time:** the editor starts empty and the tests are the ones you passed in the lesson.
